subject: RE: FinTechCo - logging controls & sensitive-data redaction (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: logging controls & redaction (next steps)

Hi Samir / Lena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end related to the logging / PII concerns you raised: 

- Scope: you flagged request/response logs (bodies + headers), trace IDs, and any header-based identifiers as sensitive for your environment.
- Redaction model: Redwood supports configurable redaction at the serving layer (regex and structured-field redaction) and optional application-layer masking before logs reach our runtime.
- Retention & residency: logs are retained per-customer; default retention is 30 days for request traces, configurable up to 90+ days on Dedicated/Private. Data residency options available in our US and EU regions.
- Auditability: audit logs show who changed redaction rules and when; we can provide weekly exports if you need them for compliance.

Attachments: I attached our redwood-logging-controls.pdf (summary of controls and sample redaction rules).

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm which fields you consider PII/PHI in your payloads (examples are helpful) — Samir, you mentioned full_name, account_number, and email in today’s call.
2) If you’re open, let’s schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) to walk your infra team through live examples and our masking configs.
3) We’ll fill out the SOC2 questionnaire you shared and return it with any evidentiary artifacts.

I’ll leave this thread open and loop in Aditya to coordinate timelines.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the recap and doc. A few clarifying questions from our security team before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) Request/response bodies: can Redwood be configured to never persist full request/response bodies for certain endpoints? For example, our /payments/POST endpoint must never store full_card_number or CVV.
2) Headers & trace ids: we use a proprietary trace id in headers to correlate requests across systems. Can we have that value obfuscated in all logs while still keeping a stable mapping for investigations (i.e., reversible by our ops with a key)?
3) Redaction rules: do you support both regex and JSON-path (structured) redaction? Are Redaction configs versioned/auditable?
4) Retention and export: if we need 7 years of certain audit artifacts for compliance, how do you support long-term retention and secure exports?

Attaching the SOC2 questionnaire we referenced — SOC2-questionnaire.xlsx — can you have Legal/Security complete sections 3–5?

- Samir
Samir Desai
Security Lead, FinTechCo

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging controls & redaction (next steps)

Samir — great questions, quick answers below and proposed actions.

1) Never-persist endpoints: yes — Redwood allows per-route persistence policies. You can set endpoints to zero request/response persistence so no bodies are written to disk or log store. For Dedicated/Private customers we can enforce that at the node level.

2) Headers & trace IDs: we support two approaches — a) deterministic hashing (one-way) that preserves correlation without reversibility, and b) reversible tokenization using a customer-managed KMS key (requires Private/Dedicated with KMS integration). We’ll outline options in the technical doc.

3) Redaction rules: we support both regex and JSONPath/field selectors. Rules are versioned and stored in the control plane; every change generates an audit entry (who, when, previous/next). We can export the rule history for your auditors.

4) Retention & exports: out-of-the-box retention is 30/90 days depending on plan. For 7-year retention we recommend an archival export workflow (S3 with encryption + customer retention policy). For Dedicated/Private we can enable long-term cold storage and automated secure exports.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll have Legal/Security (Aditya) fill sections 3–5 of your SOC2 sheet.
- Schedule the technical deep-dive: I can do Tue/Wed next week; please confirm times that work for your infra team.

If helpful, we can prepare a short demo showing: sample payload redaction in-flight, header masking, and an example of a reversible tokenization flow with KMS.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
